note: CUT 63727 -> 63712 (-15, all in `schema`) by F787: the `questions` item schema's two decide-only sub-fields now lead with `decide ONLY:` so an ask_user batch is not offered a field askfields._DECIDE_ONLY refuses (folder-reorg:20261027-170451 turn 48 lost a turn to it), and the parent description stopped enumerating the per-question sub-fields the item schema already declares. The clarification is net-free: it pays for itself twice over. PREVIOUS: RAISED 62345 -> 63727 (+1382: +1008 `schema`, +374 `harness`) for D212 increment (a): one `ask_user` action may ask SEVERAL questions, and every filed decision record carries its CLASS. The cost is three things a run cannot use the feature without: the `questions` field's ask_user clause (the batch exists to be asked for), the new `blocks_work` field (the class override, whose description has to state the test it claims — `without this answer the run cannot do the work it was fired to do` — AND that it is not `mode`, because confusing the recorded class with the waiting mode is the one misreading that would make a run park itself), and the harness bullet that tells a run the batch exists at all. The first draft cost +2667; it was cut to this by dropping the justification prose from the bullet, shortening both clauses, and leaving the per-question sub-fields declared but undescribed (they mean for their question exactly what the same-named top-level field means, the way decide's items are already undescribed). What it buys back is measured, on the asking side rather than the contract: 37% of runs (60 of 163 over 282 real question records) already asked more than one question, up to 6, one action and one turn each, at a median 430 tokens of question prose per ask — so a run that batches 3 asks saves 2 turns of its own context, which is larger than 1382 chars, and the operator gets one grouped card set instead of 3 unrelated ones (51% of his answering sittings already disposed of several at once). `python tests/test_prompt_budget.py --update` refuses to raise, deliberately: this was a hand edit, and the next CUT should lock itself in with that command. PREVIOUS: RAISED 61821 -> 62345 (+524, all in `schema`) for D118 phase 3: the `background` field's description is the only place a run learns WHICH kinds may be deferred and what the ordering promise is, and phase 3 made three mutations deferrable behind a dependency barrier (engine/background_order.py). A run that is not told a write may defer, that touching the declared target is held until it lands, that a second deferred write to one target is refused and that a `then_script` may not ride a deferred change cannot use the feature safely — and the previous wording actively forbade it (`NOT available on a WRITING KIND`), so the engine accepted what every model was told to refuse.
